notes.meaning: The angels gathered once again before the Lord to give an account of their service. Satan also came among them, intending to present himself and make a fresh report. Even the greatest enemy of God must appear before His throne and answer to Him.

The Lord asked Satan where he had been, though God already knew all things. Satan answered that he had been wandering back and forth across the earth. His answer reveals that he is restless and never idle in his search to cause trouble.

The Lord pointed out Job to Satan again, praising him as a blameless and godly man who has no equal on earth. Even after losing his wealth and his children, Job held tightly to his faith and honest character. God noted that Satan had urged attacks against Job even though Job had done nothing to deserve such ruin.

Satan replied with a common proverb about trading one skin for another. He argued that a man will gladly let go of all his possessions and even his family as long as his own body is kept safe. In Satan's cynical view, Job's devotion was purely selfish.

Satan dared God to strike Job's actual body, touching his bones and flesh with terrible sickness. He claimed that if Job suffered severe physical pain, he would openly curse God to His face. The devil believed that intense bodily agony would finally destroy Job's faith.

The Lord gave Satan permission to afflict Job's body, but He set a strict boundary. Satan was ordered to spare Job's life and could not kill him. This shows that the devil's power is always held in check by God's sovereign command.

Satan left the Lord's presence and struck Job with painful, burning sores from head to foot. The disease covered his whole body, leaving no part free from agony. This terrible affliction showed how cruel Satan can be within the limits God allows.

Job sat down in an ash heap, showing his deep sorrow and humble condition. He took a piece of broken pottery to scrape his running sores and find relief from the awful itching. Having lost his comforts and helpers, he bore his pain with quiet endurance.

Job's wife could no longer stand the sight of her husband's misery and urged him to give up his pure walk with God. She told him to curse God and die so his suffering would finally end. In her grief and anger, she tempted Job to do the exact thing Satan had predicted.

Job corrected his wife, telling her she was talking like one who does not understand God's ways. He asked whether people should welcome only good gifts from God and refuse to accept hard trials. In the middle of all this crushing pain, Job guarded his tongue and said nothing sinful.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teachers argue that Job brought his suffering on himself by speaking words of fear, but the Bible text directly states that Job did not sin in what he said.

notes.meaning: Three of Job's close friends, known for their wisdom and high standing, heard about the terrible disasters that had crushed him. They traveled from their separate lands and agreed to meet so they could go together to comfort him. Their long journey showed their sincere love and desire to share his grief.

When the friends saw Job from a distance, he was so disfigured by his disease that they could hardly recognize him. They broke out in loud weeping, tore their robes, and threw dust into the air over their heads. These actions were traditional ways to express deep sorrow and heartbreak.

The friends sat on the bare ground with Job for seven days and nights without saying a word. They remained quiet because they saw how overwhelming his pain and misery were. Sitting in silent companionship was their way of showing true sympathy during a time of great mourning.
